finding: shipments.csv is Latin-1, not UTF-8
decision: Read with the encoding it is stored in; the failure is demonstrated in the opening cell

finding: products.csv carries a byte-order mark
decision: Read with utf-8-sig; tested rather than assumed — pandas strips it either way

finding: Rows copied whole
decision: Removed. 1,458 rows in the file, 1,440 shipments described

finding: The same shipment entered twice under a second id
decision: Removed the re-entered copy, keeping the row in the file's own id sequence

finding: Four date formats mixed row by row
decision: Detected by pattern, then parsed per row rather than per column

finding: Slash dates readable day-first or month-first
decision: Resolved from evidence inside each row, never by assumption

finding: Rows with no decisive evidence at all
decision: Settled by the order of events, then by the PO number; the two methods agreed on all 11 rows where both applied

finding: Shipments whose own timeline is impossible
decision: Flagged and excluded from every timing figure until someone rules on them

finding: Supplier codes failing an exact match
decision: 16 tidied, 7 had the hyphen restored, 6 recovered from the loading port, 8 left unresolved

finding: Product codes matching nothing
decision: Left flagged; the join shows them empty rather than guessing a product

finding: A code written 27 ways for 8 ports
decision: Normalised against the master with accents stripped; 12 spellings collapse to 3 Mexican ports

finding: Rows where an independent test disagrees with the code
decision: Listed with the reason each was caught: matching nothing, a different tariff code, or a price far from the master's

finding: Declared HS codes contradicting the product master
decision: 6 carry the same duty rate and cost nothing; 16 disagree on the rate and are itemised below

finding: Shipments where the code and the duty paid cannot both be right
decision: The money identified which field is wrong: 12 tariff codes, 4 SKUs pointing at the wrong product

finding: Duty the declared codes imply beyond what was paid
decision: MXN 1,207,422 of exposure if the declaration is read literally — corrected by fixing the codes

finding: Amounts stored as text
decision: 2,380 flags across three patterns, but only 1,291 distinct cells: 1,033 carry a currency symbol, 1,291 a thousands separator, 53 are written the European way

finding: Broken spreadsheet formulas
decision: '#REF!' in the customs processing fee, left missing rather than filled with zero

finding: Lines breaking quantity x price = total
decision: 3 with a zero quantity and 3 with a price 100x too high; identified by cause, not corrected

finding: Shipments with a missing timing figure
decision: Reported, never estimated — a blank date is an absent fact

finding: Supplier delivery performance
decision: No difference is detectable (chi-square p = 0.118). No ranking published, because none is supported
